units.source_statement: In the house-entry continuation Jupiter or Venus, one or both in the tenth house, signifies a fair opening to the door.
preconditions: Jupiter/Venus in tenth.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Distinct from planets directly in fourth or a general benevolent planetary aspect.

units.source_statement: Saturn in tenth is said to mean the opening is near a ditch, pit or deep place.
preconditions: Saturn in tenth.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source says door opening, not the stored goods themselves.

units.source_statement: Mars in tenth is said to place the entrance near making fire, slaughter/killing beasts, or heading them.
preconditions: Mars in tenth.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Three historical examples; not a real fire or animal death.

units.source_statement: Mercury in tenth is said to mean the door opening near where the household master stores instruments or tools used around beasts.
preconditions: Mercury in tenth.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Specific instrument-storage premise; not any written paper.

units.source_statement: Sun in tenth is associated with a stool, seat or bed near the entrance.
preconditions: Sun in tenth.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Source local architectural analogy only.

units.source_statement: For the Moon in the tenth, Lilly places the entryway near a door under the ground or another frequently used household feature, giving a furnace or a quern (hand grain mill) as examples.
preconditions: Moon in tenth in this printed house-entry subsection.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Original PDF388/printed354 reads 'as a Furnace or Querne, or such like'; earlier editorial 'oven' was incorrect. Do not merge this with other Moon-based location sections.
units.original_page_anchor: as a Furnace or Querne, or such like

units.source_statement: The heading asks what was stolen according to the lord of the second or tenth house.
preconditions: A stolen-goods question, with appointed house ruler.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Printed marginal note qualifies this as more properly decided by the SECOND lord.

units.source_statement: The first planetary inventory associates Saturn with lead, iron, azure/black/blue, wool, black garments, leather, heavy things and earth-working tools.
preconditions: Saturn identified as the relevant second (or heading's tenth) ruler.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Original source materials list; not a verified inventory.

units.source_statement: The planetary inventory associates Jupiter with oil, honey, quinces, silk and silver.
preconditions: Jupiter is relevant goods-signifier in the heading's method.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not merge these with Jupiter-as-general-fortune inference.

units.source_statement: The inventory associates Venus with white clothes, white wine and green colour.
preconditions: Venus is relevant goods-signifier.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Gendered material symbolism not empirical.

units.source_statement: Mars is linked to pepper, armour, weapons, red wine, red clothes, brass, war horses and hot items.
preconditions: Mars relevant goods-signifier.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not interpret as evidence of weapon possession.

units.source_statement: Mercury is linked to books, pictures and implements or other associated goods.
preconditions: Mercury relevant goods-signifier.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The later quality inventory additionally mentions money and paper; preserve separately.

units.source_statement: Sun is linked to gold, oranges, brass, carbuncles and yellow garments.
preconditions: Sun relevant goods-signifier.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Source material analogies, not an identified stolen object.

units.source_statement: Moon is linked with ordinary and common commodities.
preconditions: Moon relevant goods-signifier.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The next page continues with beast/animals and other categories.

units.source_statement: The heading The quality of the Goods stolne opens a separate second-lord classification.
preconditions: This is a duplicate thematic method with different items and explicit second-lord preference.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Original margin says some judgments work more in countryside than city.

units.source_statement: With Saturn as second lord the source suggests lead, iron, kettle with three feet, black clothing, hide or animal skin.
preconditions: Saturn rules SECOND house specifically, not a planet anywhere in chart.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The original class includes material and artifact alternatives.

units.source_statement: With Jupiter as second lord Lilly suggests a white object such as tin, silver, variegated yellow/white or broadcloth.
preconditions: Jupiter as second-house ruler.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Source's colour examples, not evidence the good was silver.

units.source_statement: With Sun as second lord the source suggests gold, precious things or other objects of good value.
preconditions: Sun as second-house ruler.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Not necessarily identical list to first goods table.

units.source_statement: With Mars as second lord the source suggests fiery objects, swords, knives or weapons.
preconditions: Mars as second-house ruler.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No factual weapon identification.

units.source_statement: With Venus as second lord the source suggests things belonging to women: rings, fair garments, smocks, waistcoats or petticoats.
preconditions: Venus rules second.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Historical gendered object classification.

units.source_statement: With Moon as second lord the source suggests beasts: horses, mules, cows or poultry, especially in the country.
preconditions: Moon second-house lord; country/urban qualification from printed margin.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not infer animal health or actual theft of livestock.

units.source_statement: The goods-quality inventory continues with Mercury signifying money, books, paper, pictures and garments of various colours.
preconditions: Mercury as second-house ruler.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is continuation of printed p354 goods list; not a separate independent method.

units.source_statement: A separate heading A signe of recovery introduces a compressed list of supposedly excellent recovery configurations.
preconditions: The source labels the list as proven; no independent outcome records supplied.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: A marginal instruction restricts the list to SIGNS OF SHORT ASCENSIONS.

units.source_statement: Moon in seventh trine to first lord is one of Lilly's listed recovery testimonies.
preconditions: Moon in seventh and trine to ascendant lord.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Source does not say mere Moon in seventh always works.

units.source_statement: Venus or the second-house lord being in the ascendant is given as recovery testimony.
preconditions: Either Venus or lord2 is in first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source's punctuation warrants caution whether conjunction or separate alternatives.

units.source_statement: Jupiter in second, direct, is listed as a separate favourable recovery indicator.
preconditions: Jupiter is in second AND direct.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Source's word direct is essential.

units.source_statement: Venus as lady of second in the ascendant appears as a more specific recovery testimony.
preconditions: Venus is ACTUALLY the second lord and in first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Different from Venus simply in first regardless of rulership.

units.source_statement: Moon in tenth trine to a planet occupying the second is included as a recovery sign.
preconditions: Moon physically tenth and trine to a planet physically second.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No arbitrary Moon-to-lord2 substitution.

units.source_statement: Moon in second trine to the second lord is separately listed.
preconditions: Moon in second; trine to lord2.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The paragraph lists alternatives, not a composite requiring the prior tenth configuration.

units.source_statement: Moon in second square Sun in twelfth is listed, somewhat unexpectedly, among the author's recovery testimonies.
preconditions: Moon in second and Sun in twelfth, square aspect.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Don't silently repair this adverse-looking square into a trine.

units.source_statement: Ascendant lord physically in second is given as another recovery testimony.
preconditions: Ascendant lord in second.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is a distinct named house position.

units.source_statement: Sun and Moon in trine are named as a recovery testimony.
preconditions: Specific solar-lunar trine.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No independent empirical support.

units.source_statement: Sun and Moon trine with the CUSP of second house is listed as an additional claim.
preconditions: Original source wording can be read as Sun and Moon both trining the cusp; verify exact syntax before automation.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Not interchangeable with Moon trine the lord of second.

units.source_statement: Second lord in fourth OR in querent's house (ascendant) is the list's last position condition.
preconditions: Lord2 in fourth or first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Original body names querent's house = first.

units.source_statement: Lilly's original marginal note says these otherwise praised recovery rules must be judged in SIGNS OF SHORT ASCENSIONS.
preconditions: Applies to preceding 'A signe of recovery' collection.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not claim all listed positive examples apply in all signs.

units.source_statement: Another separate heading If it shall be recovered introduces deeper Moon-term/house-lord procedures.
preconditions: A source question whether stolen substance returns.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Keep distinct from previous short-ascension proof list.

units.source_statement: Lilly calls the lord of the Moon's TERM the significator of the stolen substance to be recovered.
preconditions: Calculate Moon's exact term ruler for specified horoscope.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Moon's domicile ruler and its term ruler are separate bodies/roles.

units.source_statement: If Moon's term lord and Moon's domicile lord BOTH increase in motion and number and are free of infortunes, Lilly predicts goods recovered whole and nothing diminished.
preconditions: Both named lords, increase in BOTH motion and 'number', and absence of affliction.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is strong source claim, not measured completeness.

units.source_statement: Lilly instructs to examine the ruler of the planetary hour in the same manner as the Moon's term ruler.
preconditions: The house/hour lord calculation is available.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not treat this as independent evidence or silently replace Moon-term ruling.

units.source_statement: Application of first lord TO Moon's term lord OR TO second-house lord, OR relevant reverse application, is another recovery channel.
preconditions: Directed applying aspect between those named significators.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Original enumerates alternatives; record direction and target.

units.source_statement: Moon applying to both of the relevant lords OR to her own domicile lord is another source recovery condition.
preconditions: Moon must be applying; original qualified 'them both' differs from one arbitrary planet.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Keep alternative and non-independence.

units.source_statement: Source adds a more complicated branch involving Sun applying to its own lord and the Moon diminished in light, with the Moon's term lord and relevant house lords also applying.
preconditions: The source's explicit diminished-Moon qualifier and signifier names need preserving.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Syntax is nested and source image may support more than one clause attachment; keep uncertain instead of broadening.

units.source_statement: The author says the recovery conclusions are especially strong when the relevant planet significator is in an angle or succedent house.
preconditions: Qualified recovery combinations already met; angularity/cadency additional.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not make angularity alone sufficient for recovery.

units.source_statement: Continuation says if the Moon's term/house ruler or second-house ruler applies to ascendant lord, the thing lost shall be recovered.
preconditions: One of the designated lost-thing significators applies to first lord.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This finishes sentence from p389; do not attribute it to all planets.

units.source_statement: Moon or first lord applying to ascendant, or either applying to second-house lord or Moon-term lord, is said to support recovery through diligent search.
preconditions: Specific applicant and target; original gives multiple alternative contacts.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: A claim of retrieval after inquiry/search is not actual verified recovery.

units.source_statement: When BOTH lunar-term ruler and Moon's domicile ruler diminish in motion or number the author predicts much of the property lost and not recoverable.
preconditions: Both distinct lunar rulers and diminution.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Contrasts with both increasing, which the author repeats just below.

units.source_statement: The page repeats that Moon-term and Moon-house rulers increasing in number and motion, safely apart from infortunes, predict complete restoration.
preconditions: Both named lords increasing and free from malefics.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: An editorial repetition of p389, not independently witnessed recovery.

units.source_statement: Under the recovery claim, the author says significators NOT cadent from angles imply soon recovery; if they are IN angles, recovery is described as moderate in time.
preconditions: Retain the unusual printed contrast between not-cadent and in-angles.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not silently standardize timing based on later astrology conventions.

units.source_statement: A new heading It what time it shall be recovered opens degree-to-time conversion.
preconditions: Requires earlier recovery significators and a perfecting aspect.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Separate whether-recovered from how-soon procedure.

units.source_statement: Lilly instructs counting degrees between the TWO planets that signify the actual recovery, then translating degrees to hours, days, weeks or years.
preconditions: Two specific planets and directed application, not generic zodiac gap.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The mapping depends on where the planets are placed.

units.source_statement: Movable signs are said to require the shorter time, indicated in weeks or months.
preconditions: Both recovery significators / their applying configuration in the specified movable signs.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not extrapolate to fixed seven-day increment.

units.source_statement: Fixed signs are said to signify months or years until claimed recovery.
preconditions: Specified source sign category.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is not a calibrated modern time prediction.

units.source_statement: Common signs are assigned a time between the movable and fixed extremes.
preconditions: Common sign condition.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The text does not give exact number of months absent degrees and other conditions.

units.source_statement: A recovery significator quick in motion is said to hasten return.
preconditions: A specific relevant significator moving swiftly.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Not the same as merely in movable sign.

units.source_statement: The source also describes significators falling from angles as shortening the delay before recovery.
preconditions: The planets that signify recovery are falling away from angles.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This can seem contrary to other angular rules and needs contextual preservation.

units.source_statement: Lilly warns his timing judgments here belong PROPERLY to this stolen-goods chapter and must not be applied indiscriminately to other inquiries.
preconditions: The immediate recovery-timing rules are being interpreted.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: An explicit scope restriction, not an optional aside.

units.source_statement: A separate heading Aphorismes concerning Recovery begins near the bottom of PDF390.
preconditions: The source changes from general timing procedure to an additional unnumbered list.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The opening printed sentence continues onto original PDF391.

units.source_statement: The first aphorism starts with eighth lord in ascendant or with ascendant lord, but its consequent appears on the following page.
preconditions: Heading and antecedent only visible on PDF390.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not invent the missing consequent or classify it as a full condition until PDF391 is read.
